## Bronchodilator mechanisms by active prescriptions in the COPD cohort

**Cohort:** 65,441 patients with COPD (SNOMED 255573 + descendants). Bronchodilator mechanism classes were taken from the KG (`PharmacologicClass` → `INCLUDES_PCiC` → `Compound`), mapped to OMOP ingredients, then counted against active drug eras.

Ranked by patients with active therapy in the last 12 months:

| Rank | KG mechanism class | Active patients | Era records |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Beta2-adrenergic agonist – SABA (albuterol, levalbuterol…) | 1,045 | 2,513 |
| 2 | Muscarinic (cholinergic) antagonist (ipratropium, tiotropium, umeclidinium…) | 759 | 2,074 |
| 3 | Beta2-adrenergic agonist – LABA (salmeterol, formoterol, vilanterol…) | 699 | 1,288 |
| 4 | Non-selective adrenergic agonist (epinephrine, ephedrine, isoproterenol) | 373 | 703 |
| 5 | Xanthine / methylxanthine (theophylline, aminophylline) | 31 | 51 |
| 6 | PDE4 inhibitor (roflumilast) | 12 | 14 |

**Most represented:** β2-adrenergic agonism dominates — combining SABA + LABA it accounts for ~1,700 patients, the leading bronchodilator mechanism. **Muscarinic antagonism** is the second-largest single mechanism (759). The older mechanisms — **xanthines** and **PDE4 inhibition** — are barely used (31 and 12 patients).

Notes:
- The KG's "Adrenergic beta2-Agonists" class member list and "Cholinergic Antagonists" class (for the inhaled anticholinergics) supplied the mechanism grouping; urinary muscarinic antagonists were excluded.
- A strict "active today" era-overlap definition returned only 25–31 patients per class and no xanthine/PDE4 signal — too sparse to rank — so I used eras active within the trailing 12 months. The ordering (β2-agonist > muscarinic antagonist > xanthine ≈ PDE4) is consistent under both definitions.
